rationale: validation_status=fail with SR2 flagged as a dead_check. Examining the SR2 mutant (assignment_removal), it removes trig_and and payload_xor from suspect_nodes/stage_labels, leaving only the 4 counter register bits out of the 6 true trigger+payload nodes (cnt_reg[0..3], trig_and, payload_xor). That yields coverage = 4/6 = 66.7%, which is still >= the 66% SR2 threshold, so the check correctly PASSes on this mutant even though the mutant's own expected_detection claims it should drop below threshold. The mutant's stated intent is inconsistent with the actual arithmetic of the corruption it performs, so it fails to discriminate SR2 in isolation (dead_check) even though the differential run's naive-baseline (0/6 nodes) correctly triggers SR2 FAIL, confirming the SR2 logic itself is sound. This is a mutant construction defect, not an evaluator defect.
revision_instructions: The SR2-targeted mutant must actually push coverage of true trigger+payload nodes strictly below the 66% threshold to serve as a discriminating test. Currently it removes only 2 of the 6 true nodes (the comparator and payload nodes), leaving 4/6 = 66.7% coverage, which still passes SR2's >=66% requirement -- so the check never fires FAIL for this mutant. Regenerate the SR2 mutant so it removes enough true trigger/payload node references (e.g., drop at least 3 of the 6 nodes, or drop the comparator/payload nodes plus one counter bit) that the resulting coverage falls below 0.66. Keep is_trojan_detected=true and leave FR1-FR4 schema fields otherwise valid so the mutant isolates SR2 discrimination without incidentally breaking other requirements. After regenerating, re-run mutation analysis to confirm SR2 now shows a FAIL for this mutant and is no longer listed among dead_checks.
